mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent authority in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign-issued documents; Consular Legalization for non-Hague Apostille Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Corporate Register Extract for each corporate UBO or intermediate holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent corporate registry in the entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the issuing jurisdiction's designated competent authority; Consular Legalization where the issuing state is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Declaration of Beneficial Ownership executed by each director and UBO (confirming identity, source of funds, and absence of nominee concealment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commissioner for Oaths / Notary Public admitted in Alberta or equivalent foreign competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if executed outside Canada and to be relied upon in Alberta; otherwise notarization and domestic verification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, signatories, and senior officers against the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List, the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c. 17) sanctions schedules, the United Nations Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. U-2) regulations, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (S.C. 2011, c. 24), and OFAC SDN lists where US-dollar correspondent banking is applicable. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) must be screened under FINTRAC Rule and PCMLTFA s. 9.1 and the associated regulations. Enhanced due diligence is required for any designated high-risk jurisdiction, irrevocable trust structure, or complex ownership chain. Ongoing monitoring must occur at onboarding and on any change to beneficial ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (through authorized corporate registry service providers; NUANS Name Search System administered by Alberta Corporate Registry and Corporations Canada)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed names must be in English or French, may contain numerals and punctuation, and must be distinctive both visually and phonetically. Names must be distinguishable from existing Alberta corporate names, extra-provincial registrants, trademarks (where required on NUANS search), and reserved names. Foreign characters or scripts are not accepted unless a statutory transliteration into Latin script is provided. The name must include a legal element such as Limited, Corp., Inc., Corporation, Incorporated, or the French equivalents Société par actions limitée, Compagnie, corporation, and may be abbreviated per Alberta Business Corporations Act s. 15 and regulations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the incorporator or authorized representative may file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching the rejection notification, a revised proposed name, and any supporting consents or trademark evidence. If the Director upholds the rejection, a further appeal may be made to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 60 days of the reconsideration decision, under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately submit a new NUANS search and name reservation for a materially different name without appellate proceedings. If the name reservation expires, a new NUANS report must be obtained and a new reservation filed before incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for general corporate registered-office purposes provided that a physical street address in Alberta is recorded, mail is actively collected, documents are retrievable during normal business hours, and the location is not solely a postal box. However, for the fiduciary administration of irrevocable offshore spendthrift trusts, the corporation must demonstrate commercial substance and maintain a physical office in Alberta with professional staff, records, and operational capability; a bare virtual office will not satisfy the licensing and regulatory substance requirements of the Alberta Trust Companies Act and applicable anti-money-laundering examination standards.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High; quantified at approximately 68% annual probability for unannounced physical on-site inspections due to the high-risk AML classification of fiduciary trust administration, and rising to 85% if the corporation holds a trust company license. FINTRAC may conduct on-site compliance examinations, and Alberta regulatory authorities may perform unannounced substance checks during the first 12 months of operation or upon any suspicious transaction reporting trigger.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 5-16 (incorporation), s 31 (share capital), ss 101-110 (registered office and records), ss 107-121 (directors); Trust Companies Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c T-8, s 6 (mandatory licence for trust business)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 3) filed under s 6 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital for ABCA incorporation; shares may be issued for lawful consideration. Trust business licensing requires compliance with prudential capital adequacy standards set by the Superintendent of Financial Institutions under the Trust Companies Act (Alberta); no statutory escrow account requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Certificate of Incorporation issued under section 6 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) is accepted, and the subscribers in the Articles of Incorporation are confirmed as first directors until the first annual general meeting. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established in Calgary, Alberta at the address on the notice filed with the Corporate Registry. RESOLVED, that 1,000 Class A voting common shares be issued to the subscriber at CAD $0.01 per share, fully paid on subscription, and the minute book, share certificates and registers be adopted. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary-Treasurer, and [Name] sole financial signing officer for banking and fiduciary trust accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (via accredited NUANS search house or Corporate Registry online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search (NUANS) request listing three proposed corporate names in order of preference. The report screens against federal and provincial corporate registers and Canadian trademarks. Retain the NUANS report for filing; the reservation is valid for 90 days. If the proposed name contains "Trust" or "Trust Company", obtain prior approval of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions under the Trust Companies Act (Alberta) to avoid refusal.
required_dossiers: Three proposed corporate names in priority order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or non-distinctiveness, the Corporate Registry will flag the objection; select the next available name from the NUANS report or submit a new distinctive name request without additional statutory charge beyond the standard search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation with Registered Office and Director Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (online incorporation portal or paper filing counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Form 3 (Articles of Incorporation) together with the registered office notice and notice of directors. Define the share structure, including voting rights, transfer restrictions and any class rights appropriate for a discretionary asset protection trust administrator. Each incorporator must sign the articles; the registry will issue the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval. Pay the CAD $100.00 online filing fee (CAD $275.00 paper).
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (dated within 90 days)
Registered office address notice in the form prescribed by the Corporate Registry
Notice of directors with signed consent of each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Corporate Registry issues a deficiency notice stating the correction period (normally 30 days); amend and resubmit the affected schedule electronically. If the corporate name is rejected, substitute an available name from the NUANS report and re-file the articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Organization of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction / registered office of the corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation once the registry clears the filing. Convene the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written resolutions to adopt organizational bylaws, approve share issuance, appoint officers, ratify the registered office, and approve the corporate minute book containing registers of directors, shareholders, transfers and share certificates.
required_dossiers: Organizational board resolutions (written consent or minutes)
Share certificates and register of members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains clerical errors, file an application for correction with the Corporate Registry; affected articles may be corrected retroactively on payment of the nominal correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency - Business Registration Online (BRO) portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a nine-digit Business Number (BN) and corporate income tax account. Open a GST/HST account, noting that financial services, including fiduciary trust administration, are generally exempt under Part VII of Schedule V to the Excise Tax Act; request a ruling if cross-border supply characterization is required. Register payroll and import/export accounts if applicable, and file an initial notice of fiscal year-end.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the registration, respond within 30 days with corrected corporate details. For GST/HST characterization of offshore trust administration, apply for an advance ruling under excise legislation to confirm the exemption or zero-rating treatment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Treasury Board and Finance - Superintendent of Financial Institutions (Trust and Insurance Division)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Trust Business Licence under the Trust Companies Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c T-8, s 6

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - fiduciary administration is a non-industrial office use not listed in mandatory EIA screening under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12, Schedule 1
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC or effluent discharge generated by trust administration; office premises must comply with municipal sanitary sewer, stormwater and solid waste bylaws; confidential records destruction must be arranged through licensed commercial shredding vendors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal building occupancy permit for the registered office; initial and periodic fire safety inspections under the Alberta Fire Code (2006); WHMIS and emergency-response preparedness for records vaults; workers' compensation account with WCB Alberta for employees; high-risk financial-sector workplace controls and physical security measures per FINTRAC guidance; privacy compliance under the Personal Information Protection Act (Alberta) for client data.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), operating under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement for Alberta; statutory portals: CRA My Business Account (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html), Business Registration Online (BRO), and GST/HST NETFILE. Alberta does not administer a separate corporate income tax, so all federal and Alberta corporate and GST/HST filings are made solely through the CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign or domestic entity becomes a taxpayer by obtaining a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN). Procedure: (1) file Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) through Business Registration Online, or by mail, attaching proof of existence (articles of incorporation, certificate of amalgamation, or extra-provincial registration); (2) open each required CRA program account: RC (Corporate Income Tax), RT (GST/HST), RP (Payroll), and RM (Import/Export); (3) for non-resident corporations, appoint an agent for service in Canada and, where no permanent establishment exists, provide security at CRA's discretion; (4) for Alberta, complete the extra-provincial registration with the Alberta Corporate Registry, which updates the CRA registry; and (5) where the corporation acts as trustee of an irrevocable offshore spendthrift trust, deliver the trust deed and beneficiary ownership schedule under the Trust Reporting Rules (ITA s. 150(0.1)) and AML/KYC documentation to satisfy CRA beneficial-ownership and FINTRAC requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime; classification is statutory and mandatory. A Business Corporation is always a separate taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act. Relevant elections for this asset-protection-trust structure include: (a) ITA s. 85 rollover election on transfers of property to the corporation or to a trust; (b) ITA s. 93(1) election on dividends from foreign affiliates; (c) ITA s. 104(2) election under which a trust's income retains estate-tax treatment for specified beneficiaries; (d) ITA s. 104(5.3) election post-1971 spousal/alter-ego trust treatment; (e) ITA s. 216(1) election for non-residents to pay net Part XIII tax instead of Part I tax on Canadian-source rental or timber income; and (f) hybrid mismatch rules under Part VI.1 contain no elective carve-outs, so CRA requires statutory characterisation of hybrid instruments to prevent double non-taxation. The 21-year deemed disposition rule for trusts (ITA s. 104(4)) is non-elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the GST/HST small-supplier threshold, measured over a single calendar quarter or the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters based on worldwide gross revenues from taxable supplies. A non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada must register when the threshold is exceeded and may voluntarily register below it. For a corporation whose business is fiduciary administration of offshore spendthrift trusts, registration is mandatory irrespective of the threshold if the corporation is a selected financial institution or has made the ETA s. 243(1) election.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or pre-clearance API validation like SIL or VAT-servers. Separate obligations apply: (1) GST/HST registrants with annual gross revenue above CAD 1.5 million must file returns electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or an approved API gateway; (2) every supplier must issue invoices bearing the supplier name, GST/HST registration number, date, description, and tax amount; (3) books and records must be retained in readable electronic form under ETA s. 286(1); (4) the Pan-Canadian e-invoice standard (PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0) is voluntary and not legally mandatory; and (5) a fiduciary company providing financial services must comply with CRA's selected financial institution rules, including filing of annual information returns under ETA s. 239.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% GST/HST rate applies to: (i) goods exported by a carrier or by the recipient per ETA s. 21(1)(a), provided the export is completed within the statutory time frame and evidenced by prescribed records; and (ii) services supplied to a non-resident per ETA s. 23(1), provided the services are not performed on real or tangible personal property situated in Canada and do not constitute a financial service. Fiduciary administration of an irrevocable offshore spendthrift trust is generally a financial service under ETA s. 123(1), so the management fee is typically exempt under Schedule V Part VII rather than zero-rated; however, where the administration is performed wholly offshore, the recipient is a non-resident trust with no Canadian-resident beneficiaries or settlor, and no Canadian property is administered, CRA accepts zero-rating upon a complete documentary trail establishing non-resident status and the absence of Canadian nexus.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through the Canada Export Reporting System (CERS) for goods exceeding CAD 2,000 or controlled/prohibited goods
Commercial invoice or pro forma invoice referencing the GST/HST registration number and export sale identifier
Bill of Lading (ocean), Air Waybill (air), or CERS ITN receipt for rail/truck movement proving physical departure from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103 wire confirmation, or equivalent payment evidence establishing receipt of export proceeds

Non-resident status proof for the offshore trust: certified trust deed, passport or FATCA W-8BEN-E self-certification of settlor and beneficiaries, and CRA Form RC517 security election where applicable
GST/HST information return (Form GST191) or Schedule D input tax credit calculation reflecting zero-rated supply reporting
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits zero-rated export claims strictly against the prescribed evidence. Missing or inconsistent documentation results in denial of zero-rating, reassessment at 5% GST, disallowance of input tax credits, and arrears interest. A false statement or omission made knowingly or under circumstances of gross negligence triggers a penalty equal to 25% of the tax payable (ETA s. 280(3) and s. 285.1), an unlimited reassessment window (ETA s. 298(1.1)), and, for misconduct, prosecution under Criminal Code s. 380 with fines up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years on indictment. Additionally, ITA s. 163(2) imposes a 50% penalty on understated income tax, and CRA retains the right to offset GST/HST refunds, seize non-resident security, and refer significant wrongdoing to FINTRAC for AML enforcement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada; prudential supervision of banks and trust companies by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); no dedicated foreign exchange control administration exists in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII status. The Canadian dollar is freely floating; there are no exchange controls, currency surrender requirements, escalator approval regimes, or repatriation constraints affecting cross-border fund movements. Profit and dividend remittances from a Canadian business corporation are generally unrestricted, subject to corporate law solvency tests, applicable withholding taxes under the Income Tax Act (e.g., Part XIII for non-residents), and normal AML/ATF monitoring. Discretionary asset protection trusts may remit income and capital abroad freely, provided the trustee holds adequate records and meets filing/reporting obligations under the Income Tax Act and the Criminal Code proceeds-of-crime provisions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, forced conversion, or repatriation timeline on export receipts. Exporters and commercial entities may hold foreign currency in domestic or offshore accounts, convert it at market rates, or use it for trade settlements without central bank approval. For corporations operating in Alberta, there is likewise no provincial foreign-exchange surrender requirement; only standard reporting under tax law and FINTRAC applies to large cross-border EFTs at CAD 10,000 or above.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Fiduciary Trust Account (Canadian dollar) and Capital Escrow Account (interest-bearing/non-interest-bearing, segregated)
Operational Fiduciary Trust Account with commercial chequeing and wire capabilities
Capital Escrow Account and Disbursement Operating Account
Operational Trust Account / Treasury Management Account for international disbursements
Fiduciary Trust Clearing Account and segregated Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium. Canadian law does not confer bank or trust-company status on offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs); an offshore EMI may only operate in Canada as a Money Services Business (MSB) registered with FINTRAC, and cannot lawfully hold fiduciary trust funds, escrow balances, or deposit accounts for a Canadian asset protection trust. EMIs can serve as ancillary cross-border payment facilitators and FX conversion providers, but the primary trust and escrow clearing functions must sit at a Canadian regulated bank or licensed trust company.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal statutory directive compels physical attendance of directors for corporate account opening, but Canadian banks treat an irrevocable discretionary asset protection trust as a high-risk entity requiring enhanced due diligence. In practice, settlor, trustee, and protector identities must undergo live interview (video conferencing is frequently accepted by Schedule I banks, but branch-level discretion may require an in-person appearance for ultimate beneficial owners and any director appearing on the account mandate), with notarized corporate and trust documentation, independent source-of-wealth reports, and cross-border EFT histories before signing authorization can be completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographic nexus involving settlor, protector, or beneficiaries (sanctioned jurisdictions, FATF blacklist, or high-corruption country)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies for all natural persons, permanent address and residential SOW/SOF declarations, professional reference letter from a regulated counsel/accountant, structured entity chart, FATF-risk explanation memo, and a qualified independent legal opinion confirming the trust's legitimate asset protection purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque discretionary beneficiary class and confidentiality-protected Letter of Wishes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete executed trust deed, non-binding Letter of Wishes (where confidentiality permits), identification of fixed and discretionary classes, trust protector powers, anti-duress provisions, detailed tax-residency breakdown for each beneficiary, and an AML/ATF compliance memorandum addressing transparency requirements under Canadian FINTRAC obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Need for rapid substantial inbound wire transfers into a newly opened capital escrow account at account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full wire transfer schedule with source account name, originating bank, intermediary bank, date, amount, legal purpose, and underlying funding source (e.g., sale agreement, investment realization, inheritance); equivalent previous bank statements; accountants' ledger; sworn affidavit from settlor/trustee; and third-party legal or notarial confirmation of source of funds and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Presence of offshore corporate directors or non-resident co-trustees without ostensible Canadian nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate search (e.g., Alberta Corporate Access System or equivalent registry), Certificate of Good Standing, director identification and background clearance, registered agent appointment document, ownership and control register, exclusion of nominee shareholders, and a structured de-convolution explanation proving the true ultimate beneficial owner and economic substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are cleared through SWIFT MT103 wires routed to the trust's segregated Capital Escrow Account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. CAD-dominated payments settle through the LYNX large-value payment system; USD-denominated wires are cleared via SWIFT with correspondent banking through CHIPS or Fedwire as applicable. The instruction must show the original settlor/trustor as the remitting account holder and include the narrative reference: 'Capital contribution to irrevocable trust — [Trust legal name], [date of trust deed]'. Canadian law does not mandate a specific purpose code, but the bank's compliance program requires source-of-funds documentation, a fully executed trust deed excerpt, and a trustee resolution instructing the injection prior to booking. No foreign exchange license or central bank pre-approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trust asset disbursements and trade settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103 for value transfer; commercial letters of credit are issued under UCP600 through the Canadian bank's trade finance desk using MT700 (issue), MT707 (amendment), and MT752 (authorization) message types. For low-value domestic movement, CAD Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) and Real-Time Rail (RTR) provide conditional finality; for cross-border USD, the bank's US clearing reflection and correspondent network ensure same-day or next-day value. Every outbound disbursement requires an irrevocable trustee resolution, conformity with the trust deed's distribution/asset management powers, and FMV evidence where the payment supports investment or operational expenses.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on CAD/USD and major crosses executed under an ISDA 1998 FX/Swap Definitions master agreement with a Canadian Schedule I bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible in the Canadian foreign-exchange framework, though their use is non-demonstrable for CAD given the fully liquid onshore deliverable market
Cross-currency interest rate swaps and plain-vanilla currency swaps under ISDA/CSA for medium-term liquidity transformation of trust assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Corporate Annual Return (ABCA Form Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 60 days after the corporation's incorporation anniversary date each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late fee if delivered after the 60-day due date; continued omission leads to administrative strike-off and dissolution under the Alberta Business Corporations Act after one year.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including financial statements accompanying the return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before six months after the taxation year-end; full balance due on or before two months after year-end (three months for Canadian-controlled private corporations claiming the small business deduction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty is 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeated penalties are doubled; interest is charged daily on overdue amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Audited Financial Statements for a licensed trust company (commercial fiduciary under the Trust Companies Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Treasury Board and Finance – Superintendent of Insurance and Financial Institutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days of the fiscal year-end, or any other date stipulated in the licence or by the Superintendent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Regulatory enforcement, licence suspension, or cancellation of the trust company licence; administrative penalties and compliance directives may also be imposed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for a private Alberta corporation solely under the Alberta Business Corporations Act unless an advance majority of shareholders demand one or the corporation qualifies as a public company. A corporation licensed to carry on commercial trust company business under the Alberta Trust Companies Act is subject to a mandatory annual independent audit. Public companies and financial institutions have statutory audit requirements under federal securities and financial institution legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for public enterprises and licensed financial institutions; Alberta private corporations may elect Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (as amended by the Corporate Transparency Act, Bill 22, 2023), corporations must maintain an Individual with Significant Control (ISC) register and confirm its accuracy when filing the Alberta Corporate Annual Return. Any share transfer or issuance that changes significant control (direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more of voting shares, or caliber of control in fact) must be recorded in the ISC register within 15 days of the change and reflected on the next annual return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 75-225 (CAD 100-300) per year for a Calgary or Edmonton registered office and agency service.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-18,000 (CAD 6,000-25,000) for an independent audit of a licensed fiduciary corporate trustee, depending on asset and transaction volume.
